presets.query: how do vector databases index embeddings

docs.title: Approximate nearest neighbour indexes explained
docs.excerpt: An index trades a little recall for a large cut in search time by visiting only part of the graph.

docs.title: HNSW graphs from first principles
docs.excerpt: Each layer of the graph links a node to its nearest neighbours; search descends from the sparsest layer.

docs.title: Choosing an index for embeddings
docs.excerpt: Flat indexes are exact and slow; IVF and HNSW are approximate and fast at different memory costs.

docs.title: Product quantization in practice
docs.excerpt: Splitting each vector into sub-vectors and coding them shrinks memory by an order of magnitude.

docs.title: Inverted file indexes for vectors
docs.excerpt: Vectors are bucketed by their nearest centroid, and a query scans only the closest buckets.

docs.title: Recall versus latency trade-offs
docs.excerpt: Raising the search breadth improves recall until the index degenerates into a full scan.

page.title: Approximate nearest neighbour indexes explained
lines: Exact search compares a query with every vector. That is fine for thousands of vectors and too slow for millions.
HNSW links each vector to a few close neighbours on several layers. A query enters at the top and walks down.
IVF groups vectors around centroids and scans only the nearest groups.

docs.title: Release schedule and support phases
docs.excerpt: Even-numbered majors enter long-term support in October and receive fixes for thirty months.

docs.title: Choosing a runtime version for production
docs.excerpt: Pin the active LTS line and move when the next one has had its first few patch releases.

docs.title: What changes between LTS lines
docs.excerpt: Each LTS line freezes its API surface, so upgrades are planned once a year instead of continuously.

docs.title: Maintenance mode explained
docs.excerpt: In maintenance a line receives only critical security fixes until its end-of-life date.

docs.title: Upgrading across two LTS lines
docs.excerpt: Run the test suite on the intermediate line first; most breaks come from removed deprecations.

page.title: Release schedule and support phases
lines: A new major line ships every six months. Even-numbered lines become long-term support releases.
An active LTS line receives bug fixes, security fixes and carefully chosen backports.
Maintenance lines receive critical fixes only, until their end-of-life date.

docs.title: Row level security by example
docs.excerpt: A policy is a boolean expression evaluated per row; rows where it is false are invisible to the query.

docs.title: Policies for multi-tenant tables
docs.excerpt: Key every table by tenant and compare it with a setting that the connection pool sets per request.

docs.title: Testing policies before you ship
docs.excerpt: Switch roles inside a transaction and assert which rows each role can read and write.

docs.title: Performance of security policies
docs.excerpt: Policies become part of the plan; an index on the tenant column keeps them cheap.

docs.title: Bypassing policies safely
docs.excerpt: Only table owners and roles with the bypass attribute skip policies, so keep those roles out of the app.

page.title: Row level security by example
lines: Turn on row level security per table, then add one policy for each kind of access.
A policy with a using clause filters every select, update and delete on the table.
A with check clause rejects inserts and updates that would create rows the role cannot see.
